hypothesis: A 7-day trial nurture sequence will increase trial-to-paid conversion by 15% by reinforcing key features and addressing common objections at the right moments.

updates.note: ⚠️ THIS IS AN EXAMPLE EXPERIMENT — Delete this when you create real ones. Shows how to track a drip campaign day-by-day.
Launched sequence to first cohort of 150 trial signups. Emails scheduled for days 1, 3, 5, 7.
Day 1 email: 62% open rate, 18% CTR. Subject line 'Your first win with Athena' performing well.
Day 3 email: 48% open rate, 12% CTR. Seeing drop-off — may need stronger hook. 3 replies asking about pricing.
Day 5 email sent. Added testimonial from nursing student based on early feedback. Will compare to control.

hypothesis: Targeting department chairs and academic deans on LinkedIn with case study content will generate qualified pilot interest at <$150 CAC.

result.notes: Generated 12 leads over 3 weeks. CAC higher than target ($187 vs $150 goal). Lead quality was mixed — 4 were decision-makers, 8 were individual faculty with no purchasing authority. Engagement on case study content was strong (4.2% CTR), but targeting needs refinement to filter out non-buyers.

updates.note: ⚠️ THIS IS AN EXAMPLE EXPERIMENT — Delete this when you create real ones. Shows a completed channel test with results and a Scale/Iterate/Kill decision.
Campaign launched. $500 budget, targeting: Higher Ed, Dept Chairs, Academic Deans, 25mi radius from top 50 nursing schools.
First week: 4 leads, $125 spent. CPL at $31 but quality TBD. One lead already replied — community college dean, interested in pilot.
Week 2: 5 more leads. Noticing pattern — many are individual faculty, not decision-makers. Need to tighten targeting.
Added job title exclusions to filter out 'Professor' and 'Instructor' — want chairs/deans only.
Campaign ended. Final tally: 12 leads, $500 spent, 4 qualified. Calling it 'Meh' — not bad but not scalable yet.
